extracted.intended_audience: public-relations counselors, organizers of women's clubs, educators, social-service leaders, and college administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on planning and executing propaganda/public-relations campaigns for voluntary organizations, women's clubs, educational institutions, social-service agencies, churches, and cultural enterprises. Covers tactics from staffing and events to publicity, ethical cautions, and tailoring messages to public opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish varied literature and educational materials
rubrics_metrics.description: To propagandize the National League of Women Voters has published all types of literature, such as bulletins, calendars, election information, has held a correspondence course on government and conducted demonstration classes and citizenship schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce a wide range of printed and instructional materials and run courses and demonstration classes to educate and mobilize members; use multiple media forms to reach different audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train a professional class of executive/legislative secretaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Training of a professional class of executive secretaries or legislative secretaries during the suffrage campaigns, where every device known to the propagandist had to be used to regiment a recalcitrant into peace-majority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in professional staff trained in propaganda techniques and organizational management; professional secretaries enable coordinated, disciplined campaigns across constituencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage prominent individuals for mass influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the time activities of the many prominent women who were in the suffrage campaigns and who also devoted themselves to the important drives and mass influence movements during the war. Such women as Mrs. Frank Vanderlip, Alice Ames Winter... come to mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit well-known, respected personalities to lend authority and rally public attention; prominent leaders help transfer legitimacy to the cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatize issues with tangible exhibits/demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumers' Committee of Women... rented an empty store... set up an exhibit of merchandise tagging each item with the current price and the price it would cost if the tariff went through. Hundreds of visitors to this shop rallied to the cause of the committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create concrete, visual demonstrations or exhibits that make abstract policy effects tangible to the public; such staging attracts visitors and converts interest into support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize and use clubs as channels of group leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Federation of Women's Clubs... Broadly classified, they include civic and city clubs, mothers' and homemakers' clubs, cultural clubs... The woman's club is generally effective on behalf of health education; in furthering appreciation of the fine arts; in sponsoring legislation that affects the welfare of women and children...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form or work through organized clubs to initiate, sponsor, and sustain public-good movements; clubs provide an existing, trusted channel to mobilize collective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address community needs not covered by existing agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: In these fields, the woman's club concerns itself with efforts that are not ordinarily covered by existing agencies, and often both initiates and helps to further movements for the good of the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify service gaps and design programs to fill them—this both meets needs and builds public credibility for the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create public events with broad mass appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A cooking school recently conducted by the New York Herald Tribune... held its classes in Carnegie Hall, seating almost 3,000 persons... refuting... that women in large cities are not interested in housewifery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan large-scale, attractive events (demonstrations, schools, shows) that draw crowds and media attention; choose venues and formats that maximize attendance and visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner with local media & institutions to extend reach
rubrics_metrics.description: A music club can... be of service to the community by cooperating with the local radio station in arranging better musical programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborate with radio, newspapers, schools, and other local organizations to broaden program distribution and influence; media partnerships amplify messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage the public through participatory competitions and programs
rubrics_metrics.description: A literary club... can sponsor... a competition in the public schools for the best essay on the history of the city, or on the life of its most famous son.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contests, student involvement, and community projects to stimulate local interest and participation; participatory formats build attachment to the cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentrate organized efforts on objects others ignore
rubrics_metrics.description: Just as women supplement men in private life, so they will supplement men in public life by concentrating their organized efforts on those objects which men are likely to ignore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select strategic niches or neglected issues where your constituency has natural authority or motivation—this increases impact and reduces direct competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train educators to act as propagandists
rubrics_metrics.description: The normal school should provide for the training of the educator to make him realize that his is a two-fold job: education as a teacher and education as a propagandist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include public-relations and public-education skills in teacher training curricula so educators can communicate the social value of education to the wider public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise the teaching profession's public prestige via propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: The teaching profession... has the right to carry on a very definite propaganda with a view to enlightening the public and asserting its intimate relation to the society which it serves...to insist on the idea of more adequate salaries for the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct sustained PR to improve public perceptions (status, pay, academic freedom) of educators; link public messaging to concrete policy goals like salary increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain institutional publicity offices and news bureaus
rubrics_metrics.description: Many colleges have already developed intelligent propaganda... in the form of college news bureaus... Some seventy-five of these bureaus are now affiliated with the American Association of College News Bureaus... A bi-monthly news letter is published... The Association endeavors to uphold the ethical standards of the profession and aims to work in harmony with the press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish dedicated publicity/news offices, publish newsletters, and participate in professional PR associations to coordinate messaging and press relations ethically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popularize scholarly work in dramatic, understandable form
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of our leading universities... feel that the results of their scholarly researches should... be given to the public in the dramatic form which the public can understand. Popularization of this message... was due to the initiative of... press agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate research findings into accessible narratives, human-interest angles, and dramatic presentations; hire publicity professionals to place stories in popular media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnose whether poor public image is message or substance
rubrics_metrics.description: If his institution does not produce the mental picture which it should, one of two things may be wrong: Either the media of communication with the public may be wrong or unbalanced; or his institution may be at fault.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether public misperception stems from communications strategy or actual institutional shortcomings; if the latter, change practice rather than merely amplifying PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use high-profile ceremonial acts to signal institutional standing
rubrics_metrics.description: Columbia University instituted a Casa Italiana... Harvard founded the Germanic Museum, which was ceremoniously opened by Prince Henry of Prussia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage inaugurations, named institutes, and ceremonies with notable guests to create prestige and signal cultural/academic authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure extension courses and public offerings fit desired image
rubrics_metrics.description: Many colleges maintain extension courses... if they have been badly planned, from the point of view of public relations, if they are unduly scholastic and detached, their effect may be the opposite of favorable... urge that they first be modified to conform to the impression which the college wishes to create.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review and adapt public-facing courses and programs for accessibility and image alignment before promoting them; do not advertise offerings that will reinforce an undesired impression.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-spot activities that correct public misconceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the opinion that the work of a certain institution is 80 per cent postgraduate research is false, it should be corrected by high-spotting undergraduate activities. If it is true... the most should be made of that fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either emphasize the undergraduate work or spotlight research discoveries—choose the narrative to align institutional reality with public relations objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lend faculty to public investigations to build relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Many universities now gladly lend members of their faculties to assist in investigations of public interest. Thus Cornell lent Professor Wilcox to aid the government in the preparation of the national census. Professor Irving Fisher of Yale has been called in to advise on currency matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage faculty participation in government and public-interest projects to demonstrate institutional relevance and attract public attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge ethical limits and avoid overadvertising
rubrics_metrics.description: In the ethical sense, propaganda bears the same relation to education as to business or politics. It may be abused. It may be used to overadvertise an institution and to create in the public mind artificial values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain ethical standards, avoid creating artificial valuations or deceptive overpromotion; balance publicity with substance to preserve credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose symbolic venues to increase conference authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Association for the Advancement of the Colored People... decided to dramatize the year's campaign in an annual convention... Since the purpose was to affect the entire country, the association was advised to hold it in the South... Atlanta was chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select event locations that give added legitimacy and local authority to your message—especially when countering a prevailing regional opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surround events with nationally and locally respected leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: The support of leaders of diversified groups was sought... in addition... important from the technical standpoint to secure the opinions of group leaders of the South, even from Atlanta itself, to emphasize the purposes of the conference to the entire public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invite and publicize endorsements from both national figures and sympathetic local leaders to broaden appeal and lend credibility in target regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engineer dramatic program elements and symbolic pairings
rubrics_metrics.description: The program itself followed the general scheme. Negroes and white men from the South, on the same platform, expressed the same point of view. A dramatic element was spot-lighted here and there. A national leader from Massachusetts agreed in principle and in practice with a Baptist preacher from the South.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create staged, newsworthy moments—cross-regional or cross-group pairings—that generate press interest and dramatize the thesis being advanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use press coverage plus targeted follow-up communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The public read the words and the ideas in the press of the country... Further publicity was attained by mailing reports, letters, and other propaganda to selected groups of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine earned media from events with targeted mailings and follow-up to specific stakeholder groups to convert awareness into sustained support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutionalize propaganda via committees, ads, and periodicals
rubrics_metrics.description: Many churches have made paid advertising and organized propaganda part of their regular activities. They have developed church advertising committees... Many denominations maintain their own periodicals. The Methodist Board of Publication and Information systematically gives announcements and releases to the press and the magazines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create standing committees, regular advertising plans, and official publications to sustain ongoing publicity and message control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design social-service campaigns to change habits with concrete directives
rubrics_metrics.description: A campaign for the preservation of the teeth seeks to alter people's habits in the direction of more frequent brushing of teeth. A campaign for better parks seeks to alter people's opinion in regard to the desirability of taxing themselves for the purchase of park facilities. A campaign against tuberculosis is an attempt to convince everybody that tuberculosis can be cured...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame social-service propaganda around specific, actionable behaviors and clear, persuasive messages that address practical habits and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use publicity to develop enlightened public opinion for policy reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Improvements in penological administration... are hampered by political influences. The legislature must be persuaded... for this there is necessary the development of an enlightened public opinion. 'Until such a situation has been brought about... progress in penology is doomed to be sporadic... The solution of prison problems, then, seems to be fundamentally a problem of conscientious and scientific publicity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ systematic, evidence-based publicity campaigns to educate voters and sway legislative bodies on administrative or policy reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: In art and applied art, create public acceptance via associative values
rubrics_metrics.description: When art galleries seek to launch the canvases of an artist they should create public acceptance for his works... The public must be interested by means of associational values and dramatic inspiration, which to the artist may be a very technical and abstract kind of beauty, must be made vital to the public by association with values which it recognizes and responds to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associate artistic work with familiar cultural values, inspirational narratives, or recognized authorities so that abstract aesthetic claims become meaningful to mass audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalize on authority stamps and foreign prestige to develop markets
rubrics_metrics.description: In the manufacture of American silk, markets are developed by going to Paris for inspiration. Paris can give American silk a stamp of authority which will aid it to achieve definite position in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prestige endorsements or cultural 'stamps' (e.g., foreign center of taste) to confer legitimacy on domestic products and help open markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate with industry to inject aesthetic values into mass-produced goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Business of many types capitalizes the esthetic sense to increase markets and profits... the artist has the opportunity of collaborating with industry in such a way as to improve the public taste, injecting beautiful instead of ugly motifs into the articles of common use, and, furthermore, securing recognition and money for himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partner artists with manufacturers to elevate product design, create new market differentiators based on taste, and generate income and recognition for the artist while improving public aesthetics.
